newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade deficit to shrink in May and June-CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade deficit to shrink in May and June-CNI.

text.p: Brazil should post smaller trade deficits in May and June due to higher imports of commodities, such as coffee and soybean, the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.

"The favorable trend in commodities exports is tied to the significant increases in world prices, which are maintaining the growth in the country's foreign currency revenues," the CNI said in the May edition of its bulletin Foreign Trade in Perspective.

Commodities rose the most among Brazilian exports in the first four months, jumping 31.7 percent from January-April 1996 and accounting for 27.5 percent of total exports versus 21.9 percent in the same period last year, it said.
Apart from stronger prices and higher physical exports of coffee and soybeans, the rise in commodities exports also reflects in part the effect of exemptions from the ICMS export tax, it added.
Among other export sectors, semi-manufactured products posted the worst showing, falling 3.96 percent from the same four-month period last year, CNI said.
Manufactured products also declined, slipping back 1.46 percent, in the period, reflecting the poor dynamism observed since 1996's second half, it said.
"That result is related to the greater level of internal economic activity, which diminishes the exportable suplus of goods," the CNI said.
Exports to the European union rose 6.28 percent in the first four months compared with January-April 1996 due mostly to higher sales of coffee, it said.
Sales to Mercosur continued to lead export growth, rising 21.27 percent in the period most as a result of higher sales to Argentina, especially in heavy motor vehicles, it added.
